paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Everybody in that wilderness got the cloud, the sea, the food and the drink, and most of them still fell (1 Corinthians 10:1-5). Paul says those things happened "as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did" (1 Corinthians 10:6). Being blessed doesn't mean you can stop paying attention, so "the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall" (1 Corinthians 10:12).

Now here's the good news, and I want you to hear it LOUD. "No temptation has seized you except what is common to man," and "God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear" (1 Corinthians 10:13). When you are tempted, He will also provide an escape. That means you are never trapped, and the escape is already on the counter waiting for you.

So what do you do with that? Paul says, "flee from idolatry" (1 Corinthians 10:14). You can't sit at the table of the Lord and the table of demons too (1 Corinthians 10:21). Pick one table, friend. And I'm telling you, you'll never find a better seat than the one the Lord set for you.
